jesse-rutherford.name: Jesse Rutherford
jesse-rutherford.bio: The voice and central visual presence of The Neighbourhood. Rutherford writes from somewhere between detachment and confession, and sings almost every line as if he is trying not to wake anybody.
jesse-rutherford.signature: A close-mic, half-spoken delivery that keeps the volume down and the nerve exposed.
listen: The whole delivery in one song: warm words sung cold, never once pushed.
The rare moment he lets the volume off the leash.
Sixty seconds of him introducing a character instead of himself.

zach-abels.name: Zach Abels
zach-abels.bio: A founding member whose guitar work gives the songs their haze. He plays around the vocal rather than over it, leaving the space that makes the records feel as cold as they do.
zach-abels.signature: Clipped, chiming motifs with more air than noise — the band’s West Coast contour.
listen: The muted opening figure — four bars that became a signature.
Long, clean intervals left hanging over the bass.
Guitar used as a pad rather than a lead.

jeremy-freedman.name: Jeremy Freedman
jeremy-freedman.bio: Founding guitarist. His parts sit underneath rather than on top, holding the harmonic floor while the lead guitar and the vocal take the light.
jeremy-freedman.signature: Texture and counter-line: the low harmonic weather the songs move through.
listen: The second guitar holding the harmonic floor under the hook.
Texture doing the work of an arrangement.
Where the two guitar parts finally trade places.

mikey-margott.name: Mikey Margott
mikey-margott.bio: Founding bassist. The band’s R&B and hip-hop leanings live mostly in the bass, which is why a guitar band from Ventura County has always grooved more than it should.
mikey-margott.signature: Patient, round and further forward than a rock record would usually allow.
listen: Bass carrying the melody while everything else recedes.
The clearest case of the band grooving instead of strumming.
A line that walks rather than anchors.

brandon-fried.name: Brandon Fried
brandon-fried.bio: The band’s drummer through three major eras: Wiped Out!, the self-titled record and Chip Chrome & The Mono-Tones.
brandon-fried.signature: Tight, unhurried pocket playing built for songs that never rush.
listen: Pocket playing that refuses to hurry the song.
Restraint on a track that invites a fill every bar.

bryan-sammis.name: Bryan Sammis
bryan-sammis.bio: The original drummer. He was there for both 2012 EPs, for “Sweater Weather”, and for I Love You. — the record that turned a Newbury Park band into an international one.
bryan-sammis.signature: The looser, rawer feel of the early EPs and the debut album.
listen: The looser, rawer feel of the pre-2014 band.
The opening track of the record he played on.

the-neighbourhood.name: The Neighbourhood
the-neighbourhood.bio: California alternative band formed in 2011 in Newbury Park, known for a standing black-and-white rule across everything it releases.
